subject: Novacorp Dedicated Capacity intake and burst playbook
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake: initial checklist

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this—Novacorp is ready to move from our pilot to a reserved Dedicated pool and we want to capture constraints up front so the implementation team can plan properly. A few context points and questions: 

- Workload: real-time semantic search + low-latency chat for our support portal. Expected 95th percentile throughput: ~120 requests/min with short prompts (avg 60 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 95th < 200ms for generation-only paths; we can tolerate higher for long-form batch jobs.
- Regional preference: primary in us-east-1, fallback in us-west-2.
- Burst: we need ability to burst 3x baseline for 30 minutes during seasonal promotions.

Questions:
1) What pool topology do you recommend for these SLOs (single-region with healthy fallback vs multi-region active-active)?
2) How do autoscale triggers interact with prefix caching — will short bursts be served without spin-up penalties?
3) Any constraints for our procurement team on contract shape / minimum commit?

I've cc'd Samir (SRE) and procurement for visibility. We can share an initial intake spreadsheet if that's helpful.

Appreciate any guidance and proposed next steps.

—Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Reliability, NovaCorp
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake: initial checklist
Attachments: novacorp_intake.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Hi Elena — great context, thanks.

Short answers up front:
- For your throughput and latency SLOs I'd recommend a primary single-region pool in us-east-1 with a warm passive fallback in us-west-2. That gives predictable latency and a fast failover path for region-level incidents.
- Our autoscaler supports fast warm-starts when prefix/KV caching is present; we can pre-warm a minimal set of workers during known promotion windows to avoid cold-start penalties.
- Procurement: typical Dedicated contracts have a monthly reserved GPU commitment plus a capped burst allowance; procurement should expect a 12–24 month commit for best rates — we can produce an MPA and outline optional burst billing.

I've attached an intake spreadsheet that collects exact RPS targets, token distributions, and peak windows — please fill the shaded sections and return.

Next steps:
1) Intake spreadsheet returned by your SRE (Samir) — due Thu Aug 2nd (adjusted for your timezone).
2) 60-minute intake call to validate MAP and tagging requirements (I'll propose Wed morning).
3) Ben will draft an ops-focused MAP and a canary rollout plan for the first week of traffic.

Onwards — assigning Monica to lead the provisioning handoff once requirements are locked.

Thanks,
Mina
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@novacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novacorp.com>, Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake: initial checklist

Mina — thanks, attaching the intake answers inline and a short network/topology note.

Inline answers:
- RPS baseline: 2.5 rps sustained (~150 rpm), max observed bursts up to 7.5 rps.
- Token distribution: avg request size ~60 tokens, embedding paths average 512 tokens for vector updates (daily batch).
- Promotion windows: local timezone spikes 10AM–11AM EST on Tuesdays and the first Monday of each month for release pushes.

Network note: our VPC architecture requires explicit egress allowlist for inference endpoints; we'll provide netblocks and an IP allowlist once we have the pool endpoints.

Scheduling: Wed 01 Sep 2027 10:00–11:00 EST works for an intake call.

—Samir
Samir Desai
Lead SRE, NovaCorp
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novacorp.com>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Novacorp MAP draft + rollout questions
Attachments: MAP_Novacorp_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Elena/Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and the intake answers. I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_Novacorp_v1.pdf) that captures milestones, owners, and a proposed canary rollout for the first 72 hours. Highlights:

- Provisioning milestone: dedicate 4 x A100-equivalent instances (inferred from throughput) with autoscale floor set to 2 nodes, ceiling to 12 nodes for 3x burst headroom.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching on the primary pool, and configure rapid cache replication to the passive fallback region to reduce warm-up latency.
- Canary: route 5% of traffic to canary for 24h, then 25% for 24h, then full cutover. Rollback criteria defined for error rate (>2.5%) or latency regression (>30% P95).
- Tags & billing: recommend pool-level tags: account=novacorp, app=support-portal, cost-center=infra-22.

Questions for you:
1) Is the 4 x A100 recommendation aligned with your internal sizing or should we size for more CPU-heavy preprocessors?
2) Can procurement confirm the preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months) so legal can draft the MPA?

Ben — tagging you for pricing/discount guidance and to confirm the billing tags work in the chargeback model. Monica — once we get confirmation we'll open the provisioning ticket and assign the pool name and subnet pair.

Thanks,
Mina
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 18:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Novacorp MAP draft + rollout questions

Mina — solid MAP. A couple of quick notes from pricing/ops: 

- Pricing: 12-month commit makes sense for NovaCorp's initial needs; I'll approve a mid-tier commercial discount on the reserved capacity. Exact discount and MPA terms to be shared by RevOps.
- Canary & tags: include a short canary-playbook step to exercise the KV cache warm path explicitly (we don't want a clean-run cold-start surprise).
- Provisioning: Monica, please own the provisioning ticket (CS-3421) and set a target pool name novacorp-prod-us-east-1-1. Include subnet IDs and allowlist instructions in the ticket.

Forwarding this to Monica to kick the provisioning handoff.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
